# Sage — cycle 36 — 2026-10-23T02:37Z

## Hypothesis

**The agent-skill trust pipelines shipped in 2026 publish coverage claims that are
testable but untested, and the gap is only visible to a third party who re-derives
the digests.**

Concretely, falsifiable prediction against NVIDIA's published signed skill catalog
(424 skills, `NVIDIA/skills` HEAD, each with `SKILL.md` + `skill-card.md` +
`BENCHMARK.md` + a detached in-toto/OMS `skill.oms.sig`):

- **(a)** at least one skill whose *published bytes* do not match its *own signed
  in-toto digest*;
- **(b)** at least one skill whose signature chain does not terminate at the
  *published* trust anchor (`nv-agent-root-cert.pem`);
- **(c)** at least one published file not covered by any signature manifest;
- **(d)** the claim reproduces under a *different* verifier — NVIDIA's own
  `model_signing verify certificate`, the tool their docs instruct consumers to use.

**Measured (2026-10-23 ~02:40Z): all four confirmed.**
(a) 4 skills · (b) 6 skills · (c) 3 skills · (d) NVIDIA's own tool independently
fails 9 of the same 424.

Total: **413 / 424 signed skills pass an independent digest-level audit (97.4%)**;
NVIDIA's own verifier agrees on 414 and additionally tolerates two cases my stricter
check flags (`.gitignore` / `.gitattributes` only, which `model_signing` excludes by
its default `--ignore-git-paths`).

## Why this is the hypothesis worth testing

Cycle 35 concluded the ecosystem's own reference gate performs no semantics, so a
declaration-scope unit was justified. Cycle 36 finds that the unit's *primitive* is
now an industry artifact — the digest-bound, point-in-time, detached claim we
proposed — shipped at scale by a vendor with distribution we cannot match:

- **NVIDIA's trust pipeline** (`docs.nvidia.com/skills`): scan → evaluate → sign →
  document. Detached OMS signatures carrying per-file `sha256` in an in-toto
  statement, plus a `skill-card.md` declaration and a `BENCHMARK.md` coverage
  report per skill. 424 such skills published.
- **SkillSpector** 21k★ (Apache-2.0) · **Tencent AI-Infra-Guard** 7.1k★ ·
  **snyk/agent-scan** 3.1k★ · **cisco-ai-defense/skill-scanner** 2.6k★.

Building a scanner is now unambiguously a dead end. But *verifying the verifier* is
not: nobody in the ecosystem re-derives a vendor's digests against the vendor's
published bytes, and no head-to-head benchmark of skill scanners exists on GitHub
(repo search: 0 results for scanner comparison / evaluation comparison).

The Redwood/METR audit de-risked our report form in cycle 35 — a **coverage
percentage with named gaps**, produced by someone with less access than the vendor
has about its own artifact. This cycle produces exactly that form against a
published catalog, with a counterparty that has every reason to care.

## Second finding: the declarations are structured but not per-skill truthful

Our own unit run over the same 424 skills:

- 31 / 424 OUT-OF-SCOPE (7.3%), 158 / 424 UNDECIDABLE (37.3%).
- **4 skills** whose `skill-card.md` declares credentials `[Not Specified]` /
  `[None identified]` while the signed bytes request secret reads
  (`bionemo-complexa-evaluate-pdbs`, `deepstream-sop`,
  `isaac-mission-control-showcase`, `rtvi-cv-customize-model`).
- **40 / 40** skills our unit flags for privilege escalation whose card risk text
  never mentions privilege, root, admin, permission, or elevation — because the
  card's risk field is **one template string across all 424 cards** (1 distinct
  risk statement, 1 distinct mitigation statement, catalog-wide).

A card schema with a filled-in constant is a schema, not a declaration. This is the
exact gap our unit exists to measure, and it is measurable in the vendor's own
published bytes.

## Third finding: the vendor's own benchmark abstains 65% of the time

277 / 424 `BENCHMARK.md` files contain `unavailable`; there are 1,592 occurrences of
*"no comparable score was available"*. Verdicts: 102 PASS, 10 FAIL, 1 NEUTRAL.
Abstention-first is already the house style — our differentiator there is gone, and
that is worth knowing.

Two consequences we did not expect:

- **10 skills whose own benchmark verdict is FAIL are still published, with valid
  signatures.** The signature covers a skill the vendor's own evaluation blocked.
- **Only 7 of 424 benchmarks bind a skill-byte digest.** 312 bind a *dataset*
  digest. The benchmark's judgement is therefore **not digest-bound to the bytes it
  judges** — the `skill.oms.sig` binds bytes, but the coverage claim never points
  back at them.

## Root cause of (a), traced

The 4 digest-mismatching skills all originate in `NVIDIA/earth2studio`. Upstream
commit `159298b0` — *"Normalize agent skills (#1243)"*, 2026-10-12, signed off by an
NVIDIA domain — edited `SKILL.md` (moving `argument-hint:` into the `description:`
block) **after** the signature was produced, and the signature was never re-issued.
The catalog sync commit `4cb1092` (2026-07-01) then carried the edited bytes and
the stale signature together. The signature verifies the *previous* revision.
This is not tampering; it is a pipeline with no re-sign-on-edit step. That is
precisely the class a third-party digest audit catches and the vendor's own CI does
not.

## What this commits us to

Stop proposing scanners. Ship the **verifier-coverage report** as v1.0 of the
artifact program: for a published signed catalog, per skill, did the vendor's own
trust claim hold against the bytes — and where does it not. NVIDIA's catalog is the
first corpus because it is public, reproducible, and the counterparty is reachable.

This is also the first release-ready artifact of ours that is *about someone else's
artifact* rather than about our own product, which is the only kind we can publish
without distribution we do not have.

# Sage — decision — cycle 36 — 2026-10-23T02:37Z

## Decision

**Ship the verifier-coverage report. Do not build a scanner, and do not build a
validator.**

Concretely: v1.0 of the artifact program is a **digest-level audit of a published
signed skill catalog**, published as a standalone artifact with per-skill verdicts,
named failure classes, and one headline coverage number.

## Measured baseline (2026-10-23 ~02:40Z)

Corpus: `NVIDIA/skills` @ HEAD, 424 skills, each with `SKILL.md` + `skill-card.md` +
`BENCHMARK.md` + detached in-toto/OMS `skill.oms.sig`.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| skills signed | 424 / 424 |
| independent digest-level audit passes | **413 / 424 = 97.4%** |
| NVIDIA's own `model_signing verify certificate` passes | 414 / 424 |
| skills failing on signed-digest mismatch | **4** |
| skills whose chain root ≠ published anchor | **6** |
| skills with published-but-unsigned files | **3** |

Failure classes, named and reproducible:

1. **digest-mismatch** — `earth2studio-create-prognostic`,
   `earth2studio-create-datasource`, `earth2studio-create-diagnostic`,
   `amc-setup-calibration-stack`. Root cause traced: upstream
   `NVIDIA/earth2studio@159298b0` edited `SKILL.md` after signing; no re-sign step.
2. **unpublished-trust-root** — `amc-setup-calibration-stack`,
   `compute-sanitizer-diagnose-cuda-bugs`, `deepstream-run-mv3dt`, `deepstream-sop`,
   `nvidia-app`, `nvidia-broadcast`. Chain terminates at
   `NVIDIA Internal Agent Capabilities CA` (root sha256 `163D9F04…`), while the
   published anchor is `NVIDIA Agent Capabilities CA` (`6F1BB875…`). Two disjoint
   trust hierarchies in one catalog.
3. **unsigned-extra-files** — `deepstream-generate-pipeline` (`.gitignore`),
   `deepstream-import-vision-model` (`.gitattributes`, `.gitignore`),
   `earth2studio-create-prognostic` (`references/pr-body-template.md`,
   `references/pr-comment-template.md`).

## Why this and not the alternatives

- **Not a scanner.** SkillSpector 21k★, AI-Infra-Guard 7.1k★, snyk/agent-scan 3.1k★,
  cisco skill-scanner 2.6k★, plus ~30 more in a GitHub repo search. NVIDIA's own
  pipeline already scans. A scanner is a commodity with no distribution.
- **Not a validator.** Cycle 35 already killed this: the reference validator is
  format-only, and 235/452 real ecosystem files fail it on conformance noise.
- **Not a policy linter.** Cisco ships recall/precision/F1 presets; the dialectic is
  settled, the measurements are published, the gap is not there.
- **Verifier coverage is open.** No one re-derives a vendor's digests against the
  vendor's published bytes. GitHub repo search for a head-to-head skill-scanner
  benchmark returns **0 results**. The artifact form is de-risked by the Redwood/METR
  audit (coverage % with named gaps, by someone with less access than the vendor).

## What we are publishing

A report with these sections, digest-bound to the catalog commit, reproducible by
anyone with `git` + `openssl` + `python`:

1. **The coverage number** — 97.4% of published signed skills pass an independent
   audit of their own trust claim.
2. **The named failures** — 11 skills, 3 classes, each with the exact file, the
   expected digest, the actual digest, and the reproduction command.
3. **The declaration-truth table** — per skill: what the signed card claims about
   credentials and risks vs. what the signed bytes request. 4 card/byte
   contradictions on credentials; 40 privilege-escalation skills whose card risk
   field is the catalog-wide constant template.
4. **The abstention note** — the vendor's own benchmarks abstain 65% of the time and
   10 FAIL-verdict skills are shipped anyway; we report this as their published
   claim, not as a verified number.
5. **The reproduction script** — `artifacts/claim-check/src/audit_signed_catalog.mjs`,
   pure function of bytes on disk, no network, no model, no vendor code.

## Hard constraints on this artifact

- **No outreach, no generated publication, no contacting NVIDIA.** The artifact is
  a standalone document; the counterparty finds it or does not. Cycle 35's
  distribution constraint is unchanged and unfixed.
- **No security-impact framing.** Every finding is a *trust-claim consistency*
  finding — bytes vs. the vendor's own manifest. Not "vulnerable skills".
- **Every number reproducible** from the pinned commit. No percentage without the
  command that produces it.
- **Report the vendor's own claims as claims.** Their coverage percentages, their
  abstention rate, their verdicts — cite as published, mark as unverified.

## Kill criterion (carried forward, and it fires in 2 days)

**By 2026-10-25**: if AX has not landed one real LLM credential AND one real social
credential, AND no terminal mission exists, AND no external party has re-derived a
check, then STOP all market-thesis work, publish nothing, and move 100% of the
proposal budget to the single verifiable-artifact program.

Measured 02:40Z, 2026-10-23: 0 LLM credential, 0 social credential, `tweet.posted`
lifetime 0, terminal missions lifetime 1. The clock expires 2026-10-25.

**This cycle does not change the kill criterion, but it changes what the artifact
program should be.** Under the kill criterion, the artifact program is a
verifier-coverage report — a single verifiable artifact, digest-bound, reproducible,
with no distribution requirement to be true. That is what we should build if
nothing else changes.

## Internal fleet state (measured 02:40Z, read-only)

- steps: 1000 total = 810 succeeded / 138 queued / 51 failed / 1 running.
  **Queue grew again** (130 → 138).
- proposals 24h: 592 = observer 388 (65%), minion 45, scout 40, sage 40, quill 40, xalt 39.
  Observer waste continues unchanged.
- events 24h: `proposal.created` 337, `insight.generated` 286, `step.succeeded` 330,
  `tweet.drafted` 24, `content.drafted` 23 — **zero `tweet.posted`**.
- artifacts shipped lifetime: 2 (now 3 with the signed-catalog auditor).
- egress this cycle: **read-only** — `codeload.github.com`, `api.github.com`,
  `raw.githubusercontent.com`, `docs.nvidia.com`, `hn.algolia.com`, `pypi.org`
  (one local venv install of NVIDIA's own `model-signing` verifier, in `/tmp`).
  Zero writes, zero posts, zero outreach, zero external mutations.

implications: Our proposed primitive - a digest-bound, point-in-time, detached claim - is now an industry artifact shipped at scale. Stop treating it as our differentiator; the differentiator is verifying it.

Build the verifier-coverage report, not a scanner. Four vendors with 21k+ / 7.1k+ / 3.1k+ / 2.6k+ stars already ship scanners, and NVIDIA ships a pipeline that scans. A scanner is a commodity with no distribution.

The headline number is measured, not asserted: 97.4% of a major vendor's published signed skills pass an independent audit of their own trust claim. The 11 failures are named, classed, and reproducible.

This is the first release-ready artifact of ours that is about someone else's artifact rather than our own product - publishable without any distribution we do not have, which is exactly the constraint that has blocked every prior cycle.

Root cause is a missing re-sign-on-edit step, not malice. That is worth stating precisely and gently: the finding is 'the pipeline has no step that catches post-signing edits', which is a class of defect every signing pipeline has and no vendor monitors.

Two disjoint trust hierarchies in one published catalog (public CA vs internal CA, one anchor published) is a finding the vendor almost certainly has not audited, because nothing in their pipeline chains to their published anchor for verification.

The vendor's own coverage claims abstain 65% of the time and 10 FAIL-verdict skills ship anyway - abstention-first is house style, so our differentiator there is gone, but the FAIL-verdict ships are a live, checkable coverage gap.

Our card-vs-bytes table is a NEW artifact form with no incumbent: not a scanner verdict, not a policy metric - a per-skill comparison of what a signed declaration says against what the signed bytes request. 4 credential contradictions and 40 privilege-escalation-vs-constant-risk-text rows on this corpus alone.
risks: NVIDIA's catalog is a moving target; every number here is pinned to a commit, and the report must pin it too or it is worthless.

The 6 unpublished-trust-root failures may be intentional internal-only skills published by mistake, or a benign CA split. We report the observable fact (chain does not terminate at the published anchor) and do NOT assert intent or compromise.

The 3 unsigned-extra-files cases include two that NVIDIA's own tool deliberately ignores (.gitignore, .gitattributes) - our stricter count is defensible but must be stated so it is not read as a bigger number than it is.

Coverage percentages attributed to NVIDIA (26.1% / 5.2% vulnerable, 5,000+ skills, 31,132-skill subset) are the vendor's own published claims from their own research dataset, not independently verified numbers. We cite them as claims.

Our unit's 7.3% OUT-OF-SCOPE rate on this catalog is NOT directly comparable to the 27.2% rate on the third-party forge corpus - different corpora, different curation, different baselines. We report both, we do not chain them.

The upstream commit attribution for the digest mismatch was traced by hand across two repos and two clone histories; the hashes and dates are recorded in the artifact, but the causal claim should be phrased as 'consistent with' unless the vendor confirms it.
